question: The product of two consecutive odd numbers is 323. What is the sum of the two numbers?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The product of two consecutive odd numbers is equal to (Middle Even Number)² − 1.

Middle Even Number = √(Product + 1) = √(323 + 1) = √324 = 18.

Sum of the two numbers = 2 × Middle Even Number = 2 × 18 = 36.

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Product of consecutive odd numbers = 323.

Formula: Let the two consecutive odd numbers be (x − 1) and (x + 1), where x is the middle even number.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b85fa95540fcc6fe00944357e4edfde301e5d2c45e56359f61f17206aa4a071b.png] 

⇒ (x − 1) × (x + 1) = 323

⇒ x² − 1 = 323

⇒ x² = 324

⇒ x = √324 = 18

⇒ First number = 18 − 1 = 17

⇒ Second number = 18 + 1 = 19

⇒ Sum = 17 + 19 = 36

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product of Consecutive Even Numbers

Similar to odd numbers, the product of two consecutive even numbers is (Middle Odd Number)² − 1.

Sum of Consecutive Odd Numbers

The sum of the first n consecutive odd numbers starting from 1 is always n².

Sum of Consecutive Numbers Property

The sum of any two consecutive odd numbers is always a multiple of 4 (e.g., 17 + 19 = 36, which is 4 × 9).
